why: The answer rejects braces altogether ('pointless, I never write them'), which is the MissingBraces misconception: braces are optional only when the body is a single statement, and leaving them out risks bugs when statements are added later, so the style judgement is wrong.

concepts.quote: Braces are pointless, I never write them.
concepts.why: It turns 'braces are optional for a single statement' into 'braces are never needed', which contradicts the rule that a multi-statement body needs a braced block.
It only implies one correct rule, that a single-statement if body may be written without braces, so the code is legal; it does not apply this to the code's values.
The answer makes no claim about statements.
The answer makes no claim about the template notation.
